title: SHE WAS ALONE IN THE DESERT
paragraphs: SHE WAS ALONE IN THE DESERT

And somehow…
she became the first person in Scripture to name God.
EL ROI — The God Who Sees.
Scroll-Stopping Facebook Post

She wasn’t the chosen wife.
She wasn’t the promised mother.
She wasn’t even free.

Hagar was a servant.
Used.
Discarded.
Running.
Genesis 16 tells the story most people skip.

A pregnant slave girl fleeing into the desert after being mistreated by Sarai.
No protection.
No future.
Just sand… and shame.
Imagine the silence of that wilderness.

No tribe.
No home.
No voice.
Invisible.
But heaven noticed.
Scripture says the Angel of the Lord found her by a spring in the wilderness (Genesis 16:7).

Not Abraham.
Not Sarai.
God.
He spoke her name.
“Hagar.”
Pause there.
In a world where slaves were property, God addressed her like a person.

Seen.
Known.
Valued.
And in that lonely desert moment, something stunning happened.
Hagar did what no one had done before in Scripture.
She named God.

“You are El Roi — the God who sees me.”
(Genesis 16:13)

A rejected woman…
A runaway servant…
Becomes the first person in the Bible to give God a name.
Because when the world looked away—
God looked closer.
And maybe that’s your story too.
Maybe you feel unseen.

Unnoticed at work.
Overlooked in your family.
Invisible in your pain.
Listen carefully.
The same God who found Hagar in the wilderness still walks deserts today.

He sees the tears no one else notices.
He hears the prayers whispered into pillows at midnight.
But the greatest proof that God sees us came centuries later.
At a cross.
Jesus Christ stepped into our wilderness of sin and shame.

The One who sees us…
also came to save us.
Your story is not hidden from Him.

Not your failures.
Not your wounds.
Not even the things you're afraid to say out loud.
And still—
He calls your name.

Have you ever felt unseen…
like nobody noticed your pain?
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
